title: DNA Area and NETosis Analysis (DANA): a High-Throughput Method to Quantify Neutrophil Extracellular Traps
author: Rebernick, Fahmy, et al.
materials: Human blood samples were collected into EDTA tubes and neutrophils were purified using the EasySep™ Direct Neutrophil Isolation Kit (STEMCELL Technologies, Vancouver, Canada) according to the manufacturer’s instructions. Neutrophils were determined to be 95% pure by flow cytometry. Following purification, 2.5–5 × 104 neutrophils were pipetted onto acid-washed coverslips coated with poly-L-lysine (Sigma Aldrich, St. Louis, USA) and then incubated in Roswell Park Memorial Institute (RPMI) 1640 medium for either 2 or 4 h at 37 °C, 5% CO2 followed by fixation in 70% ethanol overnight at 4 °C. Then, the neutrophils were washed with phosphate buffered saline (PBS, Corning, Corning, USA), stained with 250 nM Sytox (ThermoFisher Scientific, Waltham, USA) and washed with PBS again. Coverslips were mounted onto microscope slides with Prolong Diamond Antifade (ThermoFisher Scientific), allowed to dry, sealed with clear nail polish (Sally Hansen, New York, USA), and stored at -80 °C.

steps.title: Isolate human neutrophils
steps.instruction: Collect human blood into EDTA tubes and purify neutrophils using the EasySep™ Direct Neutrophil Isolation Kit (STEMCELL Technologies) following the manufacturer’s instructions; verify purity (~95%) by flow cytometry.

steps.title: Plate human neutrophils on coverslips
steps.instruction: Pipette 2.5–5 × 10⁴ neutrophils onto acid‑washed coverslips pre‑coated with poly‑L‑lysine (Sigma Aldrich) and incubate in RPMI‑1640 medium for 2 h or 4 h at 37 °C, 5 % CO₂.

steps.title: Fix human neutrophils
steps.instruction: Fix the cells by adding 70 % ethanol and incubating overnight at 4 °C.

steps.title: Stain and mount human samples
steps.instruction: Wash coverslips with PBS (Corning), stain with 250 nM Sytox (ThermoFisher Scientific), wash again with PBS, mount onto microscope slides with Prolong Diamond Antifade (ThermoFisher Scientific), let dry, seal with clear nail polish (Sally Hansen), and store at –80 °C.

steps.title: Isolate murine neutrophils
steps.instruction: Purify neutrophils from mouse bone marrow as described previously, confirm ~95 % purity by flow cytometry, and plate onto poly‑L‑lysine‑coated coverslips.

steps.title: Treat and incubate murine neutrophils
steps.instruction: Incubate the plated murine cells for 4 h at 37 °C, 5 % CO₂ either untreated or with 10 µg ml⁻¹ LPS ± 100 ng ml⁻¹ TNF‑α.

steps.title: Fix, permeabilize and stain murine samples
steps.instruction: Fix and permeabilize the murine neutrophils, stain with DAPI (as previously described), then mount and store exactly as for the human samples.

steps.title: Run DANA_I on image set
steps.instruction: Open all fluorescence images for a given sample in Fiji (ImageJ), run the DANA_I macro on each image (or batch‑process if <7 overlapping cells per image): convert to 8‑bit grayscale, apply threshold, run ‘Analyze Particles’ to generate ROIs with areas between 20 µm² and 3500 µm², export ROI measurements to a .csv file, and overlay numbered ROI outlines on the original image.

steps.title: Quality‑control DANA_I output
steps.instruction: Manually review the ROI overlays; discard any image where DANA_I creates seven or more ROIs containing multiple cells or fails to capture cells accurately (e.g., due to high background).

steps.title: Run DANA_II analysis
steps.instruction: Launch the DANA_II Java program, import all .csv files generated by DANA_I for the sample, and automatically eliminate ROIs whose raw integrated density falls outside the standardized cut‑offs (see step 11). For the remaining ROIs, compute the average area of the five smallest ROIs (x‑bar), calculate each ROI’s relative area (ROI area ÷ x‑bar), label ROIs as NETs when the relative area exceeds the NET cutoff, and export per‑image .csv files containing ROI area, relative area, NET status, number and percentage of NETs, and average cellular DNA area. Also export a summary .csv for the whole sample with average % NETosis and average DNA area.

steps.title: Apply sample‑specific cut‑offs
steps.instruction: For human Sytox‑stained neutrophils: exclude ROIs with raw integrated density < 20 000 (fragments) or > mean + 1.5 SD (multiples); set NET cutoff at 4.70 × the area of the five smallest ROIs. For murine DAPI‑stained neutrophils: exclude ROIs with raw integrated density < 10 000 (fragments) or > mean + 2.0 SD (multiples); set NET cutoff at 5.34 × the area of the five smallest ROIs. Include a negative control sample containing only condensed nuclei to define x‑bar.
